title.tagline: You have forty seconds. Then it all starts over, and who you were helps you.
title.online_sub: Co-op or duel over the network

1.name: The Delacroix Gallery
1.desc: A museum of glass and brass. The guards are bored; time never is.

2.name: The Saint-Ange Mansion
2.desc: A masked ball, keycards changing hands, and chandeliers that can go dark.

3.name: The Lantenac Bank
3.desc: Cameras, lasers, time locks: the house that never sleeps.

4.name: The Floating Casino
4.desc: A gambling liner moored on the river. Everyone cheats; so do you.

5.name: The Clock Tower
5.desc: Where the Watch was forged. Where it wants to go back.

ending.credits: CASSE — design, code, music: a one-person studio and its echoes. Thanks for playing.

1-1: So you're the girl who stole the Saint-Ange Watch. Do you even know what's on your wrist?
A watch that goes back forty seconds when you squeeze it. And a headache.
The Clockmakers' Consortium is combing the city for it. You need money to disappear. Start small: the Delacroix Gallery, one safe, nobody around.
1-2: A door wired to a pressure plate. Someone has to stand on it, and someone else has to go through.
Not anymore. Spend one loop on the plate; on the next one, your echo will be waiting there.
1-3: This button opens the door for three seconds only. Your echo will have to press it at the right moment… twice.
1-4: A guard. He sees far ahead of him, not behind. Watch his light on the floor: where it isn't, you're invisible.
1-5: This one never leaves his post. Unless a coin drops somewhere, far from him…
Everyone turns around for a coin.
1-6: The great hall: two doors, two plates, a guard in the middle. Tonight there will be three of you.
Three Odiles. The city isn't ready.
2-1: Hi! Milo. Basile said you needed an eye on electronic locks.
The mansion's doors open with coloured keycards. Grab one, and put it down before you crack the safe: you only have two hands.
2-2: The ball! Two guards sweep the room. But if someone stands on the cloakroom plate, the chandeliers go out.
In the dark they only see a step and a half ahead.
2-3: Miss Varenne. You have something that belongs to me.
The Consortium doesn't chase thieves. It waits for them to tire. You'll see: repeating yourself is exhausting.
Augustine Lantenac. Focus. That butler turns his back now and then: sneak up behind him and knock him out.
2-4: Two keycard doors. When a card opens a door, it closes four seconds later… unless someone stays in the doorway.
Then I'll stand in the doorways. Several times.
2-5: The ballroom floor is glass. It sings underfoot. The guards hear it three metres away.
So we make something else sing, somewhere else. A coin, Odile.
3-1: The Lantenac Bank. Where the Consortium keeps its secrets. A camera watches the hall.
This terminal cuts it for ten seconds. Hold the key to hack it.
3-2: Lasers. A button cuts them for a moment. One echo can't press it and get across.
3-3: The strongroom door opens when both its levers are pulled at once. The same second.
The clock in my head is very precise.
Watch the timeline at the bottom of the screen: it tells you where your echoes are, at every instant.
3-4: A time lock! It only opens between twenty and thirty seconds. And the camera watches the wait.
3-5: The strongroom. Three levers, three Odiles. It's the last job I need.
You need? I thought the money was for me.
4-1: Basile sold me out. Lantenac was waiting at the meeting point.
I'm sorry. But I found something on the liner: the Consortium hides the Tower's plans there.
Two cameras, two terminals. I can't cut them at once from afar. You can.
4-2: The upper deck, plunged into darkness if someone holds the plate. Three guards. One of them paces in the middle.
4-3: In the hold: a keycard behind the lasers, and the safe's door only opens with it.
4-4: The captain's safe. The Tower's plans are inside, I'm sure of it.
Two levers at both ends of the ship, a guard in the middle. I need three of me.
5-1: The plans say it all. Lantenac wants to put the Watch back into the Tower's great mechanism, at noon sharp.
The whole city would replay the same forty seconds. Forever. Debts would never come due; the Consortium would never lose a thing.
One loop for everyone. I know what that feels like. No.
The Tower's doors open in turn, like gears. Hold one open.
5-2: Odile. Wait. I… I didn't know what she meant to do with it.
You knew how much she was paying.
The pendulum guards the heart of the mechanism. The terminal cuts the camera long enough. Let me help you, one last time.

intro.text: Valmont, a rainy night. Odile Varenne breaks a museum showcase and takes the only thing still shining: a brass watch.
The glass doesn't fall. It hangs in the air. Then it rises back.
Forty seconds later, she passes herself in the corridor.
The Watch doesn't turn time back. It starts it over, and what you did there stays, right beside you.

betrayal.text: The meeting was on the quay. Basile was there. So was Lantenac.
An envelope changed hands. Odile had already rewound.

finale.text: Noon. At the top of the Tower, Lantenac waits before the dial.
Odile did not come alone. She is never really alone.
At dawn, the Watch stopped. Odile let it stop.
For the first time in weeks, the morning had only one version.
